title: comparison-columns — two offers set against one shared column of labels
idea: Two or three options set against one shared column of labels, so every row is a direct comparison on one criterion. The reader scans across, not down.
why_new: spec-table gives one label column and one value column, which describes a single thing. Nothing in the catalog sets value against value, so pricing tiers and service options are forced into equal-card-grid, where each card repeats the labels and the comparison disappears.
built_from: a stack of non-stacking three-column rows sharing one width set, plus a header row. Closest existing relative is spec-table, so it may belong in ItemPattern instead — worth deciding first.
risk: only for briefs with real parallel options and matching facts for each; an empty cell reads as a missing feature. Three columns is the hard cap, and it must become one stack per option on mobile with the labels repeated.
